notes:
## Content and page identity

The sheet bears the main-hand number **37** at the top and a thinner grey **81** at the bottom-left in a different hand. The latter is preserved as a margin number rather than the author's page number. The title is an underlined **Lemme**; the proof begins **Dém**, also with one independent underline. No date or larger work title is written on this sheet.

The lemma states an equivalence between conditions on two parts J,L of an ordered set I: they are bands with mutual lower/upper bounds, and they occur respectively as an ideal and coideal inside a band I′ whose elements lie between elements of J and L. A third condition in a) is cancelled. The page asserts uniqueness of I′ and gives the interval-hull formula labelled (67), followed by a proof. This is a description of the manuscript's claims, not a verification of the proof.

## Rereadings prompted by mathematics or notation

- The cancelled inequality was reread together with the entire cancelled condition. Its lower horizontal stroke makes it **l≤j**, not C's l<j; the long cancellation itself is a separate higher stroke.
- The b) occurrence after *idéal de* was checked because H mentions an accent/prime preceding I. The crop actually shows an elevated stroke before I **and** a clear prime after it. The candidate retains the two-stroke reading with I′ as the alternative; it does not silently decide whether the left mark is a duplicate prime.
- The whole formula (67) was inspected: the letters are i, I, j, J, l, L; the bounds are j≤i≤l; the long middle stroke is the set separator. The printed candidate does not add a condition or change the inequalities. The displayed label and the ordinary proof reference read 67 on this page. The very small interlinear reference is blotted; its 67 is deliberately uncertain and was not supplied from another page.
- Both implication arrows and both superset signs were read on the halves. All four small subscript zeros in the ideal argument were checked as j_0, and the source's a)2° reference and inserted a1° reference were distinguished.
- The final *un élément de I* was reread because the argument makes J a natural expectation. The visible I has both horizontal bars and no J descender. **I is retained as written.** This looks like a possible author slip; no correction to J has been made.
- The lower L in *L est un coidéal* is overtraced but still has the L foot. No legible previous letter was invented beneath it.

## Corrections, explicit doubts and handwriting

The author cancels the third condition in a), replaces the existence wording with the unique-band assertion, adds I′ after bande, inserts the statement about formula (67) into the opening of the proof, adds the reference (par a1°), and substitutes an interlinear par above cancelled wording near the end. These insertions are attached by their actual leaders and levels.

The repeated **petite petite** is visible across the line break and is retained. The old **une** and old second word **par** remain uncertain under crossing/overwriting. The lower connecting word **et/c'est**, the inserted **donné/donnée**, the tiny inserted **67**, and the smaller punctuation mark after i∈J remain narrow transcription doubts. These are the reader's doubts, not question marks written by the author. There is no independently legible author question or doubt annotation on this page.

The apparent final ! in the cancelled condition is read provisionally as the connected downturned endpoint of the cancellation. This departure from C is at medium confidence and has its own blind-review region. The long curved leader before prouvons is not a parenthesis. The D's extended foot is not a second underline. The marginal ie, main-text ens, and Dém have no visible final stops; qfd. has no initial c. No diagram or drawing is present. Pale incidental background texture is not transcribed.

The first reader did not perform a proof check; its mathematical observations directed visual rereading. Root subsequently performed the targeted check recorded below and in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

## Root targeted proof check

For the interval set B defined by (67), a)2 places J and L inside B. If x≤z≤y with x,y in B, choose j≤x and y≤l; then j≤z≤l, proving B is a band. Convexity of J proves its ideal property in B, and the dual proves the coideal property of L. The defining bounds supply the two cofinality requirements. Conversely, b) forces I′ to equal this interval set, giving uniqueness and the smallest-band assertion. This checks the argument on this leaf; it is not an independent re-proof or a formal certificate. The final written I supplies only the weaker assertion that i bounds an element of the ambient I; J is the letter needed to complete the stated cofinality conclusion. The clear manuscript I remains unchanged.

check_events.outcome: Checked the lemma and uniqueness against formula (67). Let B be the set of i between some j in J and l in L. Assumption a)2 gives J union L subset B. If x<=z<=y with x,y in B, choose j<=x and y<=l; then j<=z<=l, so B is a band. If x in B and x<=j in J, choose j0 in J with j0<=x; convexity of J gives x in J, hence J is an ideal of B. The dual gives L coideal. Formula (67) supplies both cofinality requirements. Under b), the band property and those requirements give exactly B, proving uniqueness and the smallest-band assertion. The final manuscript I (clear upper and lower serifs) is retained; J is needed for the stated cofinality conclusion, while I would only give a weaker tautology. This is a targeted check of the supplied argument, not an independent re-proof or formal certificate.
